## Connecting research and understanding.

I work in applied research, data science, and program evaluation in community mental health. My focus is on using data and sound research methods to understand services, examine outcomes, and support practical decisions. Measurement is an important part of that work, along with statistical analysis and clear communication of findings.

I also provide periodic guidance on doctoral psychology interns' research projects. I am developing teaching resources that use examples, explanations, and practice activities to make statistical concepts easier to understand.

## Featured publication

::: {.editorial-spotlight}

<span class="section-kicker">Peer-reviewed research · 2025</span>

<div class="spotlight-title">Telemental health and remote work: An exploratory analysis of their dual impact on mental health professionals’ experiences during COVID-19 stay-at-home orders</div>

Lizano, Bergen, Smith, Pasquarella, and Lee examine how the rapid shift to remote work and services shaped mental health professionals’ experiences, with implications for workforce well-being and clinical care.

[Read the publication](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11414-024-09925-z) · [See all publications](research.qmd)

:::

## Teaching resources in development

Elementary Statistics is the first planned course collection. I also intend to add short lectures, video explanations, and other standalone resources over time. The course roadmap is available now, but the individual lessons are still in development.
